[00:01:58] Evan Li: yeah couple things — dedicated pools give you predictable qps and routing, but cost per-token will be higher if utilization is low. we can run a burst config and autoscale; also quantized model variants can help hit that 150ms P95.
[00:02:14] Tom Beckett: can you clarify quantized variants — we have some concerns about hallucination/regression from quantization.
[00:02:22] Evan Li: totally. our Optimize team has profiles per-model; we usually run a small eval on your prompt set to measure quality delta. for critical prompts we can stick to fp16 and for lower-importance traffic run the quantized path. it's a rollout strategy basically.

[00:03:13] Sofia Andrade: we'll require VPC peering or private link; no public egress for any PHI-type payloads. also we have an internal firewall that inspects TLS — works fine but we'll need an IP set.

[00:03:34] Evan Li: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; there are a couple of options depending on whether we run in your cloud account or provide a private control plane. audit logs are shipped to S3/BigQuery — sorry sorry sometimes the auto-transcript says big-query as big quirky — but yes we can stream audit logs.

[00:03:58] Priya Nair: typically we stream events with near-real-time delivery and we keep an append-only audit trail; for tamper-evidence we can recommend using object versioning + ledgering in your storage or push to your SIEM.

[00:04:30] [00:04:30] Marta Ruiz: I heard earlier mention of KV cache, uh could you spell out how caching works with sessions? we expect long conversations so cache size and eviction matter.
[00:04:40] Evan Li: sure, we maintain KV cache per session and cache can be pinned or shared depending on routing. note sometimes the transcript shows K V cash instead of cache — transcript quirk — but the upshot: we manage KV cache to avoid re-encoding large prefixes which helps latency. wide contexts we handle by chunking and hot-swap of cache entries.

[00:05:28] Evan Li: minimal topology is VPC with peering or private link, route tables for subnets where inference nodes live, and optional NAT for ancillary services. we can also set static egress IPs for allowlisting.
